title: Dispatching economics proformas and sanity checks (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note and lightweight model (proforma) for a dispatch-centric smart-routing policy. Focus: how to mix spot/on-demand capacity across regions and fallback tiers while minimizing money spent per successful request under realistic preemption and cold-start dynamics.

Scope and constraints:
- Not an exhaustive modeling effort; goal is practical heuristics + sanity-checks for PM/infra handoff.
- Intended for product + infra to synthesize into a deployable policy prototype (canary) and a spreadsheet for exec review.
- We assume we can route at request granularity (per-request decision), and we can pre-warm a small pool per-region per-model.

Key definitions (as used in the notes):
- dispatch blend: fraction of incoming requests routed to spot capacity in a region before fallback.
- soft-preempt behavior: when spot instance is reclaimed, request either fails fast (retry) or degrades to lower-quality model; cost depends on retry path.
- effective unit cost: expected $ per successful token returned (inc. retries + prewarm amortization).

High-level hypothesis:
You can save 20–40% on unit cost for multi-tenant workloads by:
  1) routing a moderate fraction of requests (25–60%) to spot in lower-latency, lower-cost regions,
  2) maintaining tiny warm pools for tail latency-sensitive customers,
  3) using probabilistic early-fallback (i.e., start on spot, if no KV-cache hit or pre-warm, fallback to ondemand after X ms) to bound latency regressions.

Spreadsheet layout (tabs we expect):
- Inputs: per-region spot price, on-demand price, preempt rate (p_reclaim), average tokens/request, prewarm cost amortization model, cold-start latency penalty (ms), retry cost multiplier
- Scenarios: conservative / base / aggressive blends (three columns)
- Sensitivity: matrix of p_reclaim vs blend fraction, output = expected $/k tokens and median latency
- Per-tenant: knobged model where high-SLA tenants get lower blend and larger prewarm pools

Core formulas (text form for sanity checks):
- expected_cost_per_req = p_spot * (cost_spot_tokens + expected_retry_cost_if_preempt) + (1 - p_spot) * cost_on_demand_tokens + amortized_prewarm
- expected_retry_cost_if_preempt = p_reclaim * (cost_on_demand_tokens + extra_latency_penalty_cost) // simplified: assume fallback to ondemand after preempt
- amortized_prewarm = (prewarm_instance_hourly_cost * prewarm_pool_size) / (requests_per_hour_allocated_to_pool)

Baseline example (numbers, base scenario):
- average tokens = 120
- cost_spot_per_1k_tokens = $0.65
- cost_on_demand_per_1k_tokens = $1.20
- p_reclaim (spot reclaim probability within a session) = 0.04 (4%)
- blend (p_spot) = 0.45
- prewarm_pool_size = 3 instances per region for high-priority customers, amortized over 10k req/hr -> amortized_prewarm ~= $0.09/req

Compute (per 1 request):
- cost_spot_tokens = 120/1000 * 0.65 = $0.078
- cost_on_demand_tokens = 120/1000 * 1.20 = $0.144
- expected_retry_cost_if_preempt = 0.04 * (0.144 + retry_overhead_estimate($0.01)) = ~0.0059
- expected_cost_per_req = 0.45*(0.078 + 0.0059) + 0.55*0.144 + 0.09 = $0.142 (approx)
- compare to all-on-demand: $0.144 + 0.09(amortized) = $0.234 -> saving ~39% on units if amortized prewarm counted same way (note: numbers illustrative)

Sensitivity quick-checks to include in sheet:
- vary p_reclaim from 1% -> 15% and show crossover where spot no longer beneficial for tail-SLA tenants.
- vary average tokens (short chat vs long generation) — spot wins more for longer average tokens because fixed prewarm amortization is diluted.
- include region price spreads: if spot < 40% of on-demand, tolerate p_reclaim up to ~8% for base blends.

Operational heuristics (early list for playbook):
- Default blend by customer-class: free-tier 70% spot, standard 50% spot, enterprise 20% spot.
- For customers with latency SLO < 200ms tail, prewarm pool required. Minimum prewarm size computed by peak QPS and desired tail percentiles.
- Soft-fallback timeout: start on spot; if no response after T_ms (suggest 120ms for short chats), route retried request to on-demand route. This bounds TTFB regressions.
- Circuit-breaker: if regional preempt rate spikes > 3x baseline in 5-minute window, reduce blend by 50% and enlarge on-demand fallback proportionally.

Failure modes and cost leak risks:
- double-charging due to concurrent warm-up + fallback: ensure we cancel spot-in-flight work when fallback accepted.
- replays due to front-end timeouts -> increase effective token cost substantially. Add countermeasures: idempotency keys and fast cancellation signals to runtime.
- under-estimated prewarm amortization: small customers with few requests/hour may show negative ROI. Add per-tenant minimums.

Open questions / TODOs (next actions):
- run micro-sim on historical request traces (sample 72 hours) to estimate real p_reclaim and per-request preemption correlation with token-length. Owner: Marco. Due: 2026-02-24.
- prototype soft-fallback logic in routing-sim and validate latency SLOs at 95/99 percentiles. Owner: Engineering (Ethan). Due: 2026-03-10.
- produce per-region price table for all shipping regions (APAC, EU, NA) and compute break-even blends. Owner: Finance. Due: 2026-02-17.

Representative scenario table (to copy into sheet):
columns: scenario_name | p_spot | p_reclaim | avg_tokens | cost_spot_per_k | cost_on_demand_per_k | amortized_prewarm | expected_cost_per_req | notes
rows (text):
- base | 0.45 | 0.04 | 120 | 0.65 | 1.20 | 0.09 | (formula) | general-purpose mix
- aggressive | 0.65 | 0.06 | 90 | 0.50 | 1.20 | 0.04 | (formula) | cost-forward, only standard tenants
- conservative | 0.25 | 0.02 | 300 | 0.80 | 1.25 | 0.12 | (formula) | enterprise-FSLA

Short recommendations (for PM and infra):
1) Build the spreadsheet with the tabs above and populate with regional prices + historical preempt trace. Include a simple UI for per-tenant knobs.
2) Implement routing-sim experiments with the three scenarios. Capture cost/loss metrics and latency percentiles.
3) Implement a canary policy that sets default blends per-tenant class + circuit-breakers and soft-fallback timeouts. Rollout to non-enterprise customers first.
4) Instrument costs (token-level + instance-level) and surface a daily dashboard showing realized vs modeled costs and preempt rates per region.

Notes to self (informal):
- watch for correlation between high input token counts and higher preempt risk (longer sessions -> higher chance to be reclaimed). If present, bias long sessions to ondemand.
- consider 'request bundling' for tiny requests to raise avg_tokens and improve amortization of prewarm.

Appendix (quick sanity):
- If preempt rate = 0, expected_cost simplifies to p_spot*cost_spot + (1-p_spot)*cost_ond + amortized_prewarm.
- If amortized_prewarm large (small customers), spot blending may hurt. Add per-tenant opt-in.

End of WIP.
Please leave notes inline in the sheet tab 'comments' and mark rows with 'validated' when simulation done.
